newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian money market inactive as Bombay banks shut.
newsitem.headline: Indian money market inactive as Bombay banks shut.

text.p: Indian money markets were inactive on Thursday as banks in Bombay, the commercial capital, were closed for a national holiday, dealers said.
The call money rates closed higher on Wednesday on fears of liquidity tightening because of funds outflows towards a bond issue, dealers said.
They said call money ended in the 4.0-4.5 percent range after opening at Tuesday's closing levels of 0.50-0.75 percent. Stray deals were also struck at 5.0 percent, some dealers said.
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) sold 25 billion rupees of 10-year bonds issued by 25 state governments on April 30 and dealers said they expected good market response to the issue.
The RBI did not announce subscription details. Most dealers expect substantial oversubscription.
Dealers however said they expected rates to drop on Friday.
"I think rates will fall..maybe not to sub-one percent levels but certainly to around 2.0-3.0 percent on Friday," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
Call money has been below 1.0 percent in the past three weeks.
